content.formula: Verb + 了 (Completion) / Sentence + 了 (Change of State)
content.explanation: Trợ từ 了 (le) dùng để: 1) Đứng sau động từ biểu thị hành động đã hoàn thành, 2) Đứng cuối câu biểu thị sự thay đổi trạng thái hoặc một tình huống mới xuất hiện.

examples.vi: Tôi đã mua ba quyển sách. (Hành động hoàn thành)
Mưa rồi. (Thay đổi trạng thái - trước đó không mưa)

exercises.question: In the sentence '下雨了' (xià yǔ le), what does 了 indicate?
exercises.explanation: 了 at the end of the sentence indicates that it has started raining (a change from the previous state).

exercises.question: Which is the correct way to say 'I bought a book'?
exercises.explanation: To indicate action completion, place 了 directly after the verb 买.

tips: Placing 了 directly after a verb focuses on action completion.
Placing 了 at the end of a sentence focuses on a change in state or situation.
Do not use 了 in negative sentences with 没 (méi).

commonMistakes.note: Phủ định bằng 没 thì không dùng 了 ở cuối câu.

title: て形の使い方

content.formula: V(て) + ください／V(て) + います

exercises.question: What is the te-form of the verb 飲む (nomu - to drink)?

exercises.question: Translate to Japanese: 'Please read this book.'
options: この本を読んでください。
この本を読んでいます。
この本を読みてください。
exercises.explanation: V-てください is used for requests. The te-form of 読む is 読んで.

tips: Group 1 conjugates to -tte, -nde, -ite, -ide, -shite
Group 2 drops -ru and adds -te
Group 3 is irregular: suru -> shite, kuru -> kite

title: TED Talk: The Power of Habit

content.transcript: Whether it’s nail-biting, screen-time scroll-holes, or eating cookies when you aren’t hungry, we all have behaviors we’d like to change. But breaking habits is hard. That’s because habits are behaviors that have become automated. They form when we repeat a behavior in response to a specific cue until it becomes automatic. Psychologists describe this as a 'habit loop'. The loop has three parts: first, a cue, which triggers the behavior; second, the routine, which is the behavior itself; and third, the reward, which reinforces the behavior, making it more likely you'll repeat it. To break a habit, you must understand your loop, keep the cue and reward, but change the routine.

vocabulary.definition: Carried out automatically by a system or process without conscious effort.
An expert or specialist in psychology.
To strengthen or support an existing behavior or structure.
A sequence of actions regularly followed; a fixed program.

content.text: The Mediterranean diet is inspired by the eating habits of people living in countries bordering the Mediterranean Sea, such as Greece, Italy, and Spain. Rather than a strict diet plan, it represents a lifestyle characterized by high consumption of olive oil, vegetables, fresh fruits, nuts, legumes, and whole grains. Moderate amounts of fish, poultry, and dairy are included, while red meat and processed foods are kept to a minimum. Numerous scientific studies suggest that adhering to this dietary pattern can significantly reduce the risk of cardiovascular diseases, promote brain health, and support healthy weight management. Olive oil, in particular, is rich in monounsaturated fatty acids, which play a key role in lower cholesterol levels and reducing inflammation. Furthermore, this diet emphasizes eating meals with family and friends, which contributes to emotional well-being and stress reduction.

title: The History of the Internet
titleVi: Lịch sử Internet
description: Read about how the internet evolved from ARPANET to a global phenomenon.

content.text: The internet has changed the way we live, work, and communicate. Its history began in the late 1960s with a project called ARPANET, funded by the United States Department of Defense. This network allowed scientists and researchers at different universities to share information and compute resources. In the 1980s, the technology grew as more academic institutions connected. The major breakthrough came in 1989 when Sir Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web. This made the internet user-friendly by introducing websites, hyperlinks, and web browsers. By the late 1990s, the internet became a global phenomenon, transforming business, entertainment, and personal communication. Today, billions of people around the world connect to the internet daily using smartphones, computers, and other smart devices.

title: Sustainable Tourism

description: Learn about the concept of sustainable tourism and how travelers can minimize negative impacts.

content.text: Tourism is one of the world's largest industries, but it can have significant negative impacts on local environments and communities. Sustainable tourism aims to minimize these negative effects while maximizing the benefits for local residents and preserving the natural heritage. This practice involves making environmentally friendly choices, such as reducing water and energy consumption, avoiding single-use plastics, and supporting local businesses. Travelers are encouraged to respect local cultures, choose eco-friendly accommodations, and use public transportation or walk instead of renting private cars. By practicing sustainable tourism, we ensure that popular destinations remain beautiful and culturally rich for future generations. It is a shared responsibility between governments, the travel industry, and travelers themselves.

content.text: 日本庭園（にほんていえん）は、自然の美しさを狭い場所に表現した伝統的な庭です。池や石、川、そして様々な植物を使って、山や海の景色を作り出します。日本庭園にはいくつかの種類がありますが、最も有名なものの一つが「枯山水（かれさんすい）」です。枯山水は水を使わず、白い砂と石だけで水や山を表現します。お寺などでよく見られ、見る人に静かな気持ちを与えます。庭園を散歩しながら、季節ごとに変わる花や木の美しさを楽しむことができます。日本庭園は、ただ見るだけでなく、自然と人間が調和する精神的な場所でもあります。

content.text: 日本で働くとき、ビジネスマナーはとても重要です。まず、挨拶をするときは頭を下げて「お辞儀（おじぎ）」をします。お辞儀の角度は、相手や状況によって変わります。また、初めて会う人とは「名刺（めいし）」を交換します。名刺は両手で持ち、相手に文字が見えるように渡さなければなりません。そして、時間は絶対に守らなければなりません。会議の時間の５分前には準備を終わらせて待つのが基本です。日本の会社では、チームワークや他への配慮が大切にされています。これらのマナーを守ることで、仕事の人間関係が良くなります。

title: TED Talk: The Power of Vulnerability
titleVi: Bài diễn thuyết TED: Sức mạnh của sự tổn thương
description: An in-depth analysis of vulnerability, connection, and human empathy based on Brené Brown's research.

content.transcript:
One of the things that I think we all struggle with is the feeling of connection. Connection is why we're here. It's what gives purpose and meaning to our lives. This is the focus of my research. But as a researcher, I wanted to understand: what is the barrier to connection?

What I found is shame. Shame is really easily understood as the fear of disconnection. Is there something about me that, if other people know it or see it, that I won't be worthy of connection?

Underpinning this shame, this fear of not being worthy, is excruciating vulnerability. In order for connection to happen, we have to allow ourselves to be seen. Really seen.

In my years of interviewing people, I realized there is a group of people who have a strong sense of love and belonging. I call them the "whole-hearted". They live from a deep sense of worthiness.

What did they have in common? They had the courage to be imperfect. They had the compassion to be kind to themselves first and then to others. And they had connection as a result of authenticity. They were willing to let go of who they thought they should be in order to be who they were.

They fully embraced vulnerability. They believed that what made them vulnerable made them beautiful. They didn't talk about vulnerability being excruciating, nor did they talk about it being comfortable. They just talked about it being necessary.

content.transcript:
本日発表された経済見通しによりますと、世界的なインフレと金利上昇に伴い、主要国の成長率は軒並み減速する懸念が強まっています。特に原油をはじめとする資源価格の高騰は、原材料を輸入に依存する日本経済にとって深刻な打撃となっており、経常収支の悪化をもたらしています。

こうした状況下で、日本銀行は大規模な金融緩和策を維持する方針を示す一方で、金利差による急激な円安が進み、輸入コストの上昇が国内の物価高をさらに押し上げています。政府関係者は「為替相場の過度な変動は望ましくなく、投機的な動きに対してはあらゆる選択肢を排除せず適切な措置を講じる」と強調しました。

専門家は、貿易構造の多角化やエネルギー自给率の向上が急務であり、金利引き上げによる景気冷え込みのリスクとインフレ抑制のバランスをどのように取るかが、今後の最重要課題であると指摘しています。

title: Documentary: The History and Spiritual Essence of Chinese Tea Culture
titleVi: Phim tài liệu: Lịch sử và tinh hoa tâm linh của văn hóa Trà Trung Hoa
description: An advanced academic lecture on how tea evolved from medicine to a philosophical representation of Taoism and Zen.

content.transcript:
中国是茶的故乡，茶文化源远流长。在漫长的历史演变中，茶已不仅仅是一种解渴的饮料，更升华为一种精神的寄托和哲学的载体。据史料记载，茶最初是作为药物使用的，所谓“神农尝百草，日遇七十二毒，得荼而解之”。

到了唐代，陆羽撰写了世界上第一部茶学专著《茶经》，系统地阐述了茶的起源、种植、采摘和冲泡方法，标志着中国茶道的正式确立。唐宋时期，茶道与佛教禅宗深度融合，形成了“禅茶一味”的独特文化现象。品茶时讲究“静、雅、和、敬”，在清幽的茶香中领悟生命的本真与内心的宁静。

茶道不仅追求冲泡技艺的精湛，更强调人与自然的和谐共生。道家思想中的“天人合一”在茶艺中得到了完美的体现。如今，随着全球文化交流的加深，中国茶文化正走向世界，成为传播中华优秀传统文化的重要纽带。

content.explanation: Từ 有 (yǒu) dịch là 'có'. Dùng để chỉ quyền sở hữu. Trái ngược với 是 (shì) phủ định bằng 不是 (bú shì), 有 bắt buộc phải phủ định bằng 没有 (méi yǒu), không được dùng 不有.

tips: Không bao giờ nói '不有', luôn nói '没有'.
Khi dùng biểu thị tồn tại, địa điểm đứng trước 有: 'Địa điểm + 有 + Sự vật'.

commonMistakes.note: Sai ở việc sử dụng '不' để phủ định '有'.

tips: Không dùng phó từ chỉ mức độ như 很 (hěn), 非常 (fēicháng) trước tính từ trong câu so sánh chữ 比. Thay vào đó dùng 更 (gèng) hoặc 还 (hái) nếu muốn nói 'hơn nữa'.

title: Cấu trúc 〜ています (Đang làm gì đó / Trạng thái)
titleVi: Cấu trúc 〜ています (Đang làm gì đó / Trạng thái)
description: Diễn tả hành động đang diễn ra tại thời điểm nói hoặc trạng thái kéo dài.

content.formula: V-te + います / V-te + いません (phủ định)
content.explanation: Thì hiện tại tiếp diễn hoặc biểu thị trạng thái kết quả của một hành động đã diễn ra trong quá khứ.

examples.native: 私は日本語を勉強しています。
examples.ja: 私は日本語を勉強しています。
examples.vi: Tôi đang học tiếng Nhật.
Anh ấy hiện tại đang ngủ.

exercises.question: Chọn câu đúng nghĩa: 'Tôi đang ăn cơm.'
options: 私はご飯を食べています。
私はご飯を食べました。
私はご飯を食べたいです。
私はご飯を食べてください。
exercises.explanation: 食べています biểu thị hành động đang diễn ra (đang ăn).

tips: Trong văn nói giao tiếp thông thường, chữ い (i) thường được lược bỏ, ví dụ 勉強してる (benkyou shiteru).

commonMistakes.wrong: 私は本を読みますしています。

title: Cấu trúc 〜たい (Muốn làm gì đó)

content.formula: V-masu (bỏ masu) + たいです / たくないです (phủ định)
content.explanation: Thay thế đuôi ます bằng たいです để diễn tả ý muốn của bản thân. Đi kèm trợ từ が (ga) hoặc を (o).

examples.vi: Tôi muốn uống nước.
Tôi muốn đi Nhật Bản.

exercises.question: Chọn câu đúng nghĩa: 'Tôi muốn mua xe hơi.'

commonMistakes.wrong: 日本語を勉強したいですします。

content.transcript: Hello and welcome to our test preparation session. Today, we're going to go over some tips and strategies to help you prepare for your upcoming exam. First, let's talk about time management. It's essential to create a study schedule and stick to it. Make sure you allocate enough time for each subject and take regular breaks to avoid burnout. Another crucial aspect is practice. The more you practice, the more confident you'll become. Try to simulate the actual test environment by taking practice tests under timed conditions. This will help you get used to the format and the types of questions you'll encounter. Additionally, review the test format and content beforehand, so you know what to expect. Don't forget to get plenty of rest and eat well before the test day. A healthy body and mind are essential for performing well under pressure. Remember, staying calm and focused is key to achieving your goals. Take a few deep breaths, read each question carefully, and manage your time wisely. With dedication and persistence, you'll be well-prepared to tackle the test and achieve the results you desire.
